Rashi on Shabbat 58b:10:1.hebrew: הזוג והעינבל חיבור - כשהן יחד, הרי הן כלי אחד: נטמא זה, נטמא זה; הזה על זה, טהור זה. וכיון דקרי ליה חיבור, שמע מינה דכי נתפרדו, הוי כלי שניטל מקצתו; ואף על גב דהדיוט יכול להחזירו, כל כמה דלא אהדריה — לאו שלם הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:10:1.english: The bell and the clapper [are a] connection - When they are together, behold, they are one vessel: [if] this one became ritually impure, that one became ritually impure; [if one] sprinkled [purification water] on this one, that one is pure. And since [it] calls it a connection, learn from it that when they separated, it is a vessel from which part was removed; and even though a common person can restore it, as long as he has not restored it, it is not complete.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:11:1.hebrew: וכי תימא - דהאי חיבור דקאמר, הכי קאמר: אפי' מפורדים קרינן ליה חיבור, ואתא לאשמעי' דאם נתפרדו משנטמאו, לא עלו מטומאתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:11:1.english: And if you say - That this 'connection' that it states is saying as follows: even [when they are] separated, we call it a connection, and it comes to teach us that if they became separated after they became impure, they have not emerged from their impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:11:2.english: Wasn’t it taught - [This was stated] with regard to that [baraita]:

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:11:3.english: Scissors [made] of parts - Whose two blades separate.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:11:4.hebrew: ואיזמל של רהיטני - פלינה של אומנים תריסים, שנותנים האיזמל לתוך בין שני עצים העשוין לכך, ולאחר מלאכתו נוטלו ומצניעו:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:11:4.english: And the blade of a plane - *Plaine* [a plane] of craftsmen [who make] shutters, who place the blade between two pieces of wood made for this [purpose], and after his work, [the craftsman] removes it and stores it away.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:11:5.hebrew: חיבור לטומאה - ואם נטמא זה, נטמא זה:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:11:5.english: A connection for ritual impurity - And if this [part] became impure, that [part] became impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:13:1.hebrew: שלא בשעת מלאכה - הואיל ואין צריכין להיות מחוברין, הוו להו כשני כלים ואין חיבור, ואף על פי שמחוברין — דע"כ שלא בשעת מלאכה דומיא דשעת מלאכה קאמר, ובשעת מלאכה מחוברין הן, אלמא במחוברין עסקינן. וגזרו לחומרא על הטומאה דליהוי חיבור, ועל הזאה דלא ליהוי חיבור. ומשום הכי קתני: חיבור לטומאה לעולם, ואין חיבור להזאה לעולם:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:13:1.english: When not in use - Since they do not need to be connected, they have the status of two [separate] utensils and there is no connection, even though they are [presently] connected — for perforce he spoke of "when not in use" parallel to "when in use", and when in use they are connected, which proves that we are dealing with [a case where] they are connected. And [the Sages] decreed stringently regarding ritual impurity that it should be a connection, and regarding sprinkling that it should not be a connection. And on account of this, [the baraita] taught: [It is] a connection for ritual impurity in all circumstances, and not a connection for sprinkling in all circumstances.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:14:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - לא תימא: ״הואיל והדיוט יכול להחזיר״; דודאי חד מנא הואי, כדקתני בברייתא: ״הזוג והעינבל חיבור״. וכי מיפרדי — הוי כלי שניטל מקצתו, ואינו מקבל טומאה העינבל לעצמו; אבל הזוג טמא לעצמו, דלא בטל ליה מתורת כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:14:1.english: Rather, Rava said - Do not say: “[The reason is] because a common person is able to replace [it]”; for certainly they were a single vessel, as is taught in the baraita: “The bell and the clapper are a connection.” And when they are separated, it is a vessel from which part has been removed, and the clapper does not contract ritual impurity on its own; but the bell [remains] impure on its own, because it has not lost the status of a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:1:1.hebrew: ושל דלת טהור - דלת מחובר לבית הוא, שהוא חבור לקרקע, ואינו כלי לקבל טומאה, וזוג העשוי לו בטיל לגביה, כדאמרי' בריש פרקין דלעיל: כל המחובר לו — הרי הוא כמוהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:1:1.english: And that of a door is ritually pure - A door is attached to the house, which is connected to the ground, and [therefore] is not a vessel [susceptible] to contracting ritual impurity; and a bell made for it is subordinate to it, as we said at the beginning of the previous chapter: "Whatever is attached to it is like it."

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:2:1.hebrew: של דלת ועשאו לבהמה טמאה - מכאן ולהבא. ואע"פ דלא עבד ביה מעשה, אלא שחישב עליו ותלאו — ותלייה לאו מעשה היא — שכל הכלים יורדים לידי תורת טומאה במחשבה שלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:2:1.english: [A bell] of a door and he converted it for an animal [is] ritually impure - From this point forward. And even though he did not perform an action upon it, but merely intended it [for the animal] and hung it — and hanging is not [considered] an action — [it is susceptible to ritual impurity,] as all utensils descend into the category of ritual impurity through his thought.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:2:2.hebrew: של בהמה ועשאו לדלת טמא - ואפי' מכאן להבא יקבל טומאה, שאין חיבורו מעשה, עד שישנהו מכמות שהיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:2:2.english: [A bell] of an animal and he designated it for a door is ritually impure - And even from this point forward it can contract ritual impurity, as attaching it is not [considered an effective] action, until he alters it from how it was.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:2:3.hebrew: שאין עולין מטומאתן - מתורת טומאה שירדה להן. ואע"פ שעדיין לא נטמאו, משנמלך עליהן — אין עולין מלקבל טומאה אלא בשינוי מעשה:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:2:3.english: That they do not ascend from their ritual impurity - From the status of ritual impurity that descended upon them. And even though they have not yet become impure, once he changes his mind regarding them, they do not ascend from [the status of] receiving ritual impurity except through a change [effected by] action.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:3:1.hebrew: עינבל - בטדי"ל, שעשוי בתוכו להשמיע קול:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:3:1.english: A clapper - Batail [in Old French], which is made inside it to produce a sound.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:4:1.english: If it is a vessel - That one considers it an ornament.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:4:2.hebrew: עינבל משוי ליה מנא - בתמיה: משום העינבל, מי הוי תכשיט:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:4:2.english: Does a clapper render it a vessel? - [This is said] in astonishment: Does it become an ornament because of the clapper?

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:5:1.hebrew: אין - עינבל משוי ליה מנא, ולא משום תכשיט, אלא משום כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:5:1.english: Yes - The clapper makes it a vessel; and not on account of [being an] ornament, but rather on account of [being a] vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:5:2.english: Every thing that passes through the fire - [The verse] speaks of metal vessels in the episode of Midian.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:6:1.english: Say the middle clause - [Which deals with] a bell of a person.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:6:2.english: Can it become ritually impure - [Does] even [a bell] of a person [become ritually impure]?

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:1.hebrew: העושה זגין למכתשת - שמפטמין בה סממנין להקטיר לריח, דקיי"ל בכריתות (פ"א ד' ו) שהקול יפה לבשמים:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:1.english: One who makes bells for a mortar - [A mortar] in which they compound spices to burn for fragrance, as we maintain in [tractate] Keritot (chapter 1, daf 6) that sound is beneficial for spices.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:2.hebrew: ולעריסה - שהתינוק שוכב בתוכה, שקורין בירצ"ה, ותולה בו זגין לקשקש, כדי שישמע התינוק וישן:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:2.english: And for the cradle - In which the infant lies, which is called berce [cradle], and one hangs bells on it to jingle, so that the infant will hear [them] and sleep.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:3.hebrew: ולמטפחות ספרים - כשנושאין אותן לבית הכנסת, שהתינוקות של בית רבן קורין שם, מקשקשין הזגין, והתינוקות שומעין ובאין:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:3.english: And for mantles of [Torah] scrolls - When they carry them to the synagogue where the schoolchildren read, the bells ring, and the children hear and come.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:4.english: And for coverings of small children - Which they hang around their necks.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:5.hebrew: ניטלו עינבליהם כו' - (אם ניטלו קודם שנטמאו — תורת טומאה עליהם ומקבלין טומאה, כדמפרש טעמא לקמיה: מעיקרא, כי אין להם עינבל דקתני טהורין — דעדיין לא נגמרה מלאכתן; אבל משירדה להם תורת טומאה, לא בטל שם כלי מעליהם בנטילת העינבל), ואם ניטל לאחר שנטמאו — עדיין טומאתן עליהן, דלא הוי ככלי שנשבר ובטל מתורת כלי ליטהר מטומאתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 58b:7:5.english: [If] their clappers were removed, etc. - ([If the clappers] were removed before [the bells] became ritually impure, the status of ritual impurity applies to them and they can contract ritual impurity, as [the Gemara] explains the reason below: initially, when they have no clapper, where it teaches "[they are] pure," [it is] because their manufacture was not yet complete; but once the status of ritual impurity descended upon them, the designation of a vessel was not nullified from them by the removal of the clapper.) And if [a clapper] was removed after [the bells] became ritually impure, their ritual impurity still remains upon them, as it is not like a vessel that broke and lost the status of a vessel so as to be purified from its ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 58b:9:1.english: A common person - For it does not require a craftsman.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:10:1.hebrew: מתיב רבא הזוג והעינבל חיבור - פי' בקונטרס: מדקרי ליה חיבור, ש"מ דכי נתפרדו הוי כלי שניטל מקצתו, ואע"ג דהדיוט יכול להחזיר, כל כמה דלא אהדרי' — לאו שלם הוא. וקשה לר"י: דהא מעיקרא נמי הוי ידענא דהוי כלי שניטל מקצתו, ולהכי פריך: "למאי חזו?" ומשני: דודאי באפי נפשה לא חזו, לא זוג ולא עינבל, אלא משום דהדיוט יכול להחזירו. ומה שפירש נמי: "והתניא כו'" — "גבי ההיא" מספורת של פרקים, לא עיין; דההוא דזוג ועינבל משנה היא במסכת פרה (פ. "ב משנה ח), וההיא דמספורת — בתוספתא דכלים. ומפרש הרב פור"ת בשם ר' שמואל: הואיל והדיוט יכול להחזירם, ואע"ג דהשתא בלא עינבל לא חזי מידי, כיון דהדיוט יכול בקל להחזירה — כמאן דמיחברי דמי; ואם נטמא העינבל, נטמא גם הזוג, כאילו הן מחוברין. נפקא מינה: דלכשיתחברו יטמא הזוג את הנוגע בו; ומיהו בלא חיבור לא יטמא כי אם העינבל לבדו שנגע בטומאה. והכי משמע לישנא דקאמר: "וכי תימא ה"ק: אע"ג דלא מיחברי כמאן דמיחברי דמי". משמע דאביי הכי סבירא ליה, דמדתלי טעמא בחזרת הדיוט, משמע דסבר דלא חזי השתא למידי; ואי לאו כמחובר חשיב ליה, היאך יקבל טומאה, מאחר דלא חזי מידי בלא חזרה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:10:1.english: Rava raised an objection: "The bell and the clapper are a connection" - The Kuntres explains: Since it calls it a "connection," learn from this that when they were separated, it is a vessel from which a part was removed; and even though a common person is able to restore it, as long as he has not restored it, it is not complete. And the Ri finds this difficult: For from the outset we also knew that it is a vessel from which a part was removed, and that is why [the Gemara] asked: "For what are they suited?" And it answered that certainly on their own they are not suited [for anything] — neither the bell nor the clapper — but rather [it remains a vessel] because a common person is able to restore it. And as for what [the Kuntres] also explained, that "Wasn't it taught, etc." [is taught] adjacent to that [baraita about] scissors of sections — he did not examine [the matter carefully], for that [teaching] of the bell and clapper is a Mishnah in tractate Parah (ch. 12, Mishnah 8), whereas that of the scissors is in the Tosefta of Kelim. And the Rav Porat explains in the name of R. Shmuel: Since a common person is able to restore them, even though now without the clapper it is not suited for anything, since a common person is able to easily restore it, they are considered as if they are connected. And if the clapper became impure, the bell also became impure, as though they were connected. The practical difference is that when they are [later] reconnected, the bell will transmit impurity to one who touches it; however, without connection, only the clapper alone, which touched the impurity, will transmit impurity. And this is also indicated by the wording [of the Gemara] where it says: "And if you say, it is saying as follows: Even though they are not connected, it is considered as if they are connected." This indicates that Abaye holds this way; for since he made the reason dependent on reattachment by a common person, it indicates that he holds that right now it is not suited for anything, and if it were not considered as connected, how could it contract impurity, seeing that it is not suited for anything without reattachment?

Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:10:2.hebrew: מתיב רבא הזוג והעינבל חיבור - שאם נטמא זה נטמא זה. וה"מ כשמחוברים, אבל שלא בשעת חיבור — אם נטמא זה לא נטמא זה, ולא חיישינן להדיוט יכול להחזיר, דהשתא מיהא לאו מחוברין נינהו. וממשנה זו אין לנו להוכיח דמיירי בשעת חיבור, כדקאמר "וכי תימא כו'", אבל מכח ברייתא מוכיח דבשעת חיבור מיירי. ומברייתא גרידתא הוה מצי רבא לאותוביה לאביי, אלא דניחא ליה לאקשויי מהך דמיירי בזוג ועינבל בהדיא לאביי, דאיירי נמי בזוג ועינבל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:10:2.english: Rava raised an objection: "The bell and the clapper are a connection" - [Meaning] that if this [one] becomes ritually impure, that [one] becomes ritually impure. And this applies [only] when they are connected; but when not at the time of connection, if this one becomes ritually impure, that one does not become ritually impure, and we do not consider [the reasoning that] a common person is able to replace [it], since right now, in any case, they are not connected. And from this Mishnah [alone] we have no [way] to prove that it is dealing with [a case] at the time of connection, as [the Gemara] says: "And if you say, etc."; but by force of the baraita, it proves that it is dealing with [a case] at the time of connection. And from the baraita alone Rava could have objected to Abaye, except that it was preferable to him to raise an objection to Abaye from this [Mishnah], which explicitly deals with a bell and a clapper, since Abaye was also dealing with a bell and a clapper.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:11:1.hebrew: (וכי תימא כו') והתניא מספורת של פרקים ואיזמל של רהיטני - שתי ברייתות הן במסכת כלים, כל אחד בפני עצמה. וברישא קתני בהדיא, דכשאינן מחוברין מקבל כל א' טומאה בפני עצמו, וגזרו על טומאה שלא בשעת מלאכה שיהא חיבור לטומאה ליטמא זה כשניטמא זה, משום דדמי לשעת מלאכה. אבל שלא בחיבורין, משמע דאפי' גזירה דרבנן ליכא, ואם נטמא זה לא נטמא זה, דלא חייש למה שהדיוט יכול להחזירו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:11:1.english: (And if you say, etc.) "Wasn’t it taught: Scissors of parts and the blade of a plane" - These are two baraitot in tractate Kelim, each one on its own. And in the first [clause], it explicitly teaches that when they are not connected, each one contracts ritual impurity on its own; and they decreed regarding ritual impurity when not during the time of work that it should be a connection for ritual impurity, [such that] this [part] becomes impure when that [part] becomes impure, because it resembles the time of work. However, when they are not connected, it implies that there is not even a rabbinic decree, and if this [part] became impure, that [part] did not become impure, for [the law] does not take into account that a layman is able to reassemble it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:14:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא כו' - פירש בקונטרס: דטומאה לא פרח הימנו כשנפרד משקיבל, הואיל וראוי להקישו, והוה ליה ככלי (עץ) שניקב בפחות ממוציא רמון, דלא טהר מטומאה. ומשמע שרוצה לומר, דמכאן ואילך לא מקבל טומאה. וקשה לר"י: דלמה לא יקבל טומאה, כיון דנפחת פחות מכשיעור, דהוי כאילו שלם לגמרי?! ונראה לר"י, דודאי גם מקבל טומאה מכאן ולהבא. ולקונטרס דחקו לפרש כן — משום דכשלא היה להם עינבל טהורין ולא מקבלי טומאה, אף על גב דראוי להקישו. ואינו דומה: דכשלא היה בו עינבל מעולם, ודאי טהור, דכיון שעומד ליתן בו עינבל, דהא עביד לקלא, והוי גולמי כלי מתכות; אבל משנגמר, שהיה בו עינבל, אף על פי שניטל — מקבל טומאה, שלא בטל מתורת כלי שהיה עליו קודם לכן. והר"ם הביא ראיה מחמת שתפרה ושייר פחות ממוציא רמון דטהורה (חולין קלח.), אפ"ג דחמת שלם שנקרע פחות ממוציא רימון מקבל טומאה. ועוד קשה לר"י לפי' הקונטרס: דלטומאה שהיתה עליהן שלא תפרח — מהני שפיר טעמא דהדיוט יכול להחזירו, בלא טעמא דראוי להקישו, כדאשכחן בפ' שלשה שאכלו (ברכות נ:) גבי מטה, דאפי' מפורקת לא פרחה טומאה מינה, אא"כ נגנבה או שאבדה חציה, או שחלקוה אחים או שותפים, שאין סופן לחברה; ולא איצטריך כלל לטעמא דהקשה, אלא לענין לקבל טומאה מכאן ולהבא, דהאי טעמא הואיל והדיוט יכול להחזירו לא מהני לקבל בה טומאה, כדקתני התם: "החזירוה — מקבלת טומאה מכאן ולהבא". ולאביי נמי הוה בעי למימר, דמשום דהדיוט יכול להחזירו, מקבלין שניהן — זוג והעינבל — טומאה מכאן ולהבא. וריצב"א הביא ראיה לפי' הקונט': דתניא בתוספתא דמסכת כלים בפ' רשב"ג: העושה זוג למכתשת ולעריסה ולמטפחות תינוקות, ניטלו עינבליהן — טהורין, משמע דזגין טהורין. ולפירוש הקונט' ניחא דטהורין — דלא מקבלי טומאה מכאן ולהבא; אבל לפר"י קשה, אמאי טהורין? ור"י השיב, דכמה ברייתות יש בתוספתא דפליגי אש"ס שלנו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:14:1.english: Rather, Rava said, etc. - The Kuntres explained that ritual impurity does not depart from it when it was separated after having contracted [impurity], since it is fit to strike it [against earthenware], and it has the status of a (wooden) vessel that was punctured with [a hole] less than [the size of] an emerging pomegranate, which was not purified of ritual impurity. And it implies that he means to say that from now on, it does not contract ritual impurity. And the Ri finds this difficult: For why shouldn't it contract ritual impurity, since it was diminished by less than the requisite measure [for purificatory destruction of a vessel], so that it is as if it were completely intact? And it appears to the Ri that certainly it also contracts ritual impurity from now on. And as for the Kuntres, what forced him to explain thus is because when they never had a clapper, they are pure and do not contract ritual impurity, even though it is fit to strike it. But it is not comparable: for when it never had a clapper in it, it is certainly pure, because since it is destined to have a clapper placed in it — for it is made for sound — it is regarded as an unfinished metal vessel; but once it was finished, in that it had a clapper in it, even though [the clapper] was removed, it contracts ritual impurity, for it has not lost the status of a vessel that was upon it previously. And the Maharam brought proof from a wineskin that one sewed up and left [an opening of] less than [the size of] an emerging pomegranate, which is pure (Chullin 138a), even though an intact wineskin that tore [with a hole] less than [the size of] an emerging pomegranate contracts ritual impurity. And furthermore, the Ri finds it difficult regarding the explanation of the Kuntres: For regarding ritual impurity that was [already] upon them so that it should not depart, the reasoning that "an ordinary person can reattach it" is completely sufficient, without the reason that "it is fit to strike it," as we find in the chapter [entitled] Shelosha She-akhalu (Berakhot 50b) regarding a bed, that even when dismantled, ritual impurity does not depart from it unless half of it was stolen or lost, or brothers or partners divided it, where they will not ultimately reassemble it. And the reasoning of striking was not needed at all except regarding contracting ritual impurity from now on, for this reason of "since an ordinary person can reattach it" is not effective for it to contract ritual impurity [while dismantled], as it is taught there: "Once they reassembled it, it contracts ritual impurity from now on." And according to Abaye as well, he wanted to say that because an ordinary person can reattach it, both of them — the bell and the clapper — contract ritual impurity from now on. And the Ritzba brought proof for the explanation of the Kuntres, as it is taught in the Tosefta of Tractate Kelim in the chapter of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: "One who makes a bell for a mortar, or for a cradle, or for swaddling clothes of infants — if their clappers were removed, they are pure." This implies that the bells are pure. And according to the explanation of the Kuntres, it works well that they are pure — that they do not contract ritual impurity from now on; but according to the explanation of the Ri, it is difficult: Why are they pure? And the Ri answered that there are several baraitot in the Tosefta that disagree with our Shas.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:5:1.hebrew: אין כדר' שמואל כו' - דחשיב ליה כלי תשמיש דאדם משום דבעי ליה לקלא, דע"י הזוג ששומע יודע היכן בהמתו עומדת ומוצאה ע"י כך; והוי כמקל של בהמה של מתכת דטמאה, הואיל ואדם רודה בה. וכ"מ לקמן גבי בירית טהורה, דמשמיע [קול] בכלי מתכות אינו טמא אלא היכא דבעי ליה לקלא. והא דמשני: "הא דאית ביה עינבל, הא דלית ביה עינבל", ולא מחלק באית ביה עינבל בין בעי ליה לקלא בין לא בעי — אומר ר"י, דלא שכיח שיעשו עינבל אלא אם כן בעי ליה לקלא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:5:1.english: "Yes, in accordance with Rabbi Shmuel, etc." - For [the Gemara] considers it a utensil for human use because he needs it for the sound — as by means of the bell that he hears, he knows where his animal is standing and finds it through this; and it is like a metal stick for an animal, which is susceptible to ritual impurity since a person directs [the animal] with it. And so it is implied below regarding "a garter is pure," that an object that produces sound among metal vessels is not susceptible to ritual impurity unless he needs it for the sound. And as for that which [the Gemara] resolves: "This is where it has a clapper, that is where it does not have a clapper," and does not distinguish in [the case where] it has a clapper between whether he needs it for the sound and whether he does not need [it] — the Ri says that it is not common that they would make a clapper unless he needs it for the sound.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:5:2.hebrew: כל דבר אשר יבא - ואע"ג דהאי קרא לא לגבי טומאה כתיב אלא לגבי הגעלה, מסתברא דהתם אין דיבור מעלה ומוריד; ואם אינו ענין להגעלה, תנהו לענין טומאה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:5:2.english: “Every thing that passes” - And even though this verse is not written regarding ritual impurity, but rather regarding purging [vessels], it is reasonable that there, speech [i.e., producing sound] makes no difference; and if it is not applicable to purging, apply it to the matter of ritual impurity.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:9:1.hebrew: (אלא) אמר רבא הואיל ויכול להקישו - פי': מקבל טומאה הזוג, אבל עינבל, דאין ראוי להקישו — לא. ומספורת ואיזמל נמי, בלא חיבור ראויין למעין מלאכה ראשונה, ומקבלי טומאה כל אחד בפני עצמו, כדתני בתוספתא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58b:9:1.english: “(Rather,) Rava said: Since one can strike it” - Explanation: The bell contracts ritual impurity, but the clapper, which is not suited to be struck, does not. And scissors and a plane blade as well, [even] without connection, are suited for [a purpose] akin to their original function, and each one contracts ritual impurity on its own, as is taught in the Tosefta.
